title: Estimation of annual exposures and antibody kinetics against norovirus GII.4 variants from English serology data, 2007–2012
abstract: Norovirus in humans is highly contagious, causing diarrhoea and vomiting, and is especially common in young children. Winter incidence varies annually, and previous research indicates that the change of dominant norovirus variant is followed by high incidence, but having a clear mechanism to explain this observation could support better prediction of epidemics. Here we analyse unique norovirus GII.4 serology blockade data from 656 children in England collected via opportunistic sampling between 2007–2012 using a mathematical model of multi-variant antibody kinetics to infer metrics such as annual attack rates and age-specific infection rates. Analysis reveals that overall infection rates with norovirus GII.4 were 205 infections per 1000 person-years (posterior median; 95% credible intervals: 191–210) with a range across years of 36–486 infections per 1000 person-years (range of posterior medians). Infection rates were lowest in children aged under 1 year at 161 infections per 1000 person-years (95% CrI: 121–210) and highest in children aged 5 years and older, at 250 infections per 1000 person-years (95% CrI: 213–289). The annual attack rate was highest in 2002, coincident with transition of the dominant variant to Farmington Hills, and frequently observed with emergence of new variants, but not always. Parameter estimates indicate moderate evidence for the immune imprinting hypothesis: a stronger antibody response to variants encountered earliest in life. Infection rates estimated here are higher than incidence reported within similar settings based on disease only and is consistent with considerable asymptomatic infection. The combined use of multi-variant antibody data and a mathematical model provide key insights on the natural history of norovirus variants which can inform epidemic planning.

title_zh: 根据英文 血清学 数据估算 诺如病毒 GII.4 变体的年度暴露量和抗体动力学,2007-2012 年
source_body_en: Norovirus in humans is highly contagious, causing diarrhoea and vomiting, and is especially common in young children. Winter incidence varies annually, and previous research indicates that the change of dominant norovirus variant is followed by high incidence, but having a clear mechanism to explain this observation could support better prediction of epidemics. Here we analyse unique norovirus GII.4 serology blockade data from 656 children in England collected via opportunistic sampling between 2007–2012 using a mathematical model of multi-variant antibody kinetics to infer metrics such as annual attack rates and age-specific infection rates. Analysis reveals that overall infection rates with norovirus GII.4 were 205 infections per 1000 person-years (posterior median; 95% credible intervals: 191–210) with a range across years of 36–486 infections per 1000 person-years (range of posterior medians). Infection rates were lowest in children aged under 1 year at 161 infections per 1000 person-years (95% CrI: 121–210) and highest in children aged 5 years and older, at 250 infections per 1000 person-years (95% CrI: 213–289). The annual attack rate was highest in 2002, coincident with transition of the dominant variant to Farmington Hills, and frequently observed with emergence of new variants, but not always. Parameter estimates indicate moderate evidence for the immune imprinting hypothesis: a stronger antibody response to variants encountered earliest in life. Infection rates estimated here are higher than incidence reported within similar settings based on disease only and is consistent with considerable asymptomatic infection. The combined use of multi-variant antibody data and a mathematical model provide key insights on the natural history of norovirus variants which can inform epidemic planning.
abstract_zh: 诺如病毒 在人类中具有高度传染性,导致腹泻和呕吐,在幼儿中尤其常见。冬季发病率每年都会发生变化,之前的研究表明,显性发病率变异的变化之后是高发病率,但有一个明确的机制来解释这一观察结果可以支持更好地预测流行病。在这里,我们分析了独特的 诺如病毒 GII.4 血清学 封锁数据,这些数据来自 2007 年至 2012 年期间通过机会性抽样收集的 656 名英格兰儿童,使用多变体抗体动力学数学模型来推断年度发病率和特定年龄感染率等指标。分析显示,诺如病毒 GII.4 的总体感染率为每 1000 人年 205 例感染(后中位数;95% 可信区间:191-210),跨年范围为每 1000 人年 36-486 例感染(后中位数范围)。1 岁以下儿童的感染率最低,每 1000 人年有 161 例感染(95% CrI:121-210),5 岁及以上儿童感染率最高,每 1000 人年有 250 例感染(95% CrI:213-289)。2002 年的年度攻击率最高,与主要变种向法明顿山的转变同时发生,并且经常观察到新变种的出现,但并非总是如此。参数估计表明免疫印记假说有适度的证据:对生命早期遇到的变异有更强的抗体反应。这里估计的感染率高于 发病率 在仅基于疾病的类似环境中报告的感染率,并且与大量无症状感染一致。多变体抗体数据和数学模型的结合使用提供了关于 诺如病毒 变体自然史的重要见解,可以为流行病规划提供信息。

title: Profiling of antibody responses to human norovirus in animals
abstract: ABSTRACT Noroviruses are a major cause of acute gastroenteritis globally, with over 30 genotypes circulating in humans, some widespread, and others sporadically detected. Human noroviruses have been detected in a variety of animal species, raising the possibility that animals may serve as reservoirs or intermediate hosts for emerging human norovirus strains. To assess whether serology can reveal the circulation of human norovirus genotypes in animals, we analyzed antibody responses in 465 sera from 17 animal species using a previously established multiplex protein microarray containing P-particle antigens from 30 GI, GII, GIV, and GVI genotypes. High antibody titers to multiple antigens were observed in sera from cats, dogs, and several duck species, and chickens, whereas lower titers to fewer genotypes were observed in sera from rats, pigs, horses, and wild boar. Sera from macaques, sea lions, harbor porpoises, cattle, sheep, goats, and serotine bats showed low or undetectable antibody titers. Although we detected antibodies to common human genotypes in cats and dogs, antibodies in other animal species were primarily directed against sporadically reported genotypes. Ninety-five samples exhibited immunodominant responses, defined as one to three genotypes exhibiting higher antibody titers than the geometric mean of the remaining genotypes, and therefore suggestive of genotype-specific recognition. Binding-blocking assays performed on selected sera confirmed some antibody responses observed on the array. Although we find no clear evidence of human norovirus circulation in animals, the strong and broadly reactive antibody profiles observed in cats, dogs, and birds warrant further investigation. IMPORTANCE Human noroviruses have been detected in multiple animal species, raising concerns that animals could act as reservoirs or intermediate hosts for emerging human norovirus strains. However, it remains unclear whether serological responses in animals reflect true circulation of human noroviruses or instead cross-reactive antibody recognition. Using a multiplex protein microarray spanning 30 norovirus genotypes, we profiled antibody responses in sera from 17 animal species. We detected broad antibody responses in cats, dogs, and several bird species, but found little evidence of consistent norovirus genotype-specific recognition. Binding-blocking assays confirmed some of the detected antibody responses. Together, our findings suggest that most antibody responses in animals likely reflect cross-reactivity or non-specific binding rather than widespread circulation of human noroviruses.
authors: Marco W. G. van de Bildt
Joke W. B. van der Giessen

title_zh: 动物体内对人 诺如病毒 的抗体反应分析
source_body_en: ABSTRACT Noroviruses are a major cause of acute gastroenteritis globally, with over 30 genotypes circulating in humans, some widespread, and others sporadically detected. Human noroviruses have been detected in a variety of animal species, raising the possibility that animals may serve as reservoirs or intermediate hosts for emerging human norovirus strains. To assess whether serology can reveal the circulation of human norovirus genotypes in animals, we analyzed antibody responses in 465 sera from 17 animal species using a previously established multiplex protein microarray containing P-particle antigens from 30 GI, GII, GIV, and GVI genotypes. High antibody titers to multiple antigens were observed in sera from cats, dogs, and several duck species, and chickens, whereas lower titers to fewer genotypes were observed in sera from rats, pigs, horses, and wild boar. Sera from macaques, sea lions, harbor porpoises, cattle, sheep, goats, and serotine bats showed low or undetectable antibody titers. Although we detected antibodies to common human genotypes in cats and dogs, antibodies in other animal species were primarily directed against sporadically reported genotypes. Ninety-five samples exhibited immunodominant responses, defined as one to three genotypes exhibiting higher antibody titers than the geometric mean of the remaining genotypes, and therefore suggestive of genotype-specific recognition. Binding-blocking assays performed on selected sera confirmed some antibody responses observed on the array. Although we find no clear evidence of human norovirus circulation in animals, the strong and broadly reactive antibody profiles observed in cats, dogs, and birds warrant further investigation. IMPORTANCE Human noroviruses have been detected in multiple animal species, raising concerns that animals could act as reservoirs or intermediate hosts for emerging human norovirus strains. However, it remains unclear whether serological responses in animals reflect true circulation of human noroviruses or instead cross-reactive antibody recognition. Using a multiplex protein microarray spanning 30 norovirus genotypes, we profiled antibody responses in sera from 17 animal species. We detected broad antibody responses in cats, dogs, and several bird species, but found little evidence of consistent norovirus genotype-specific recognition. Binding-blocking assays confirmed some of the detected antibody responses. Together, our findings suggest that most antibody responses in animals likely reflect cross-reactivity or non-specific binding rather than widespread circulation of human noroviruses.

title: Feasibility and Usability of Self-Collected Blood Samples for Studies of Norovirus and Acute Gastroenteritis
abstract: BACKGROUND: Tasso self-collection blood kits have been validated against venous blood-derived serum samples, but not for studies of acute gastroenteritis (AGE). The authors' objectives were to describe the performance of the Tasso+ for self-collection of blood samples among adults and children enrolled in a study of medically attended AGE and to describe specimen processing and antibody testing success. METHODS: The authors used the Tasso+ device for self-collection of blood samples within a prospective cohort study at Kaiser Permanente Northwest. Serum samples were assessed for the presence of antibodies against the norovirus capsid protein. RESULTS: Of a total of 1353 adults and 93 children, 63% of adults and 61% of children returned a blood specimen. Of these, 88% were deemed viable for processing, and 100% of viable specimens were of sufficient volume and quality to be processed and assessed for norovirus antibodies. CONCLUSIONS: The results suggested that Tasso+ is a feasible blood collection tool for studies of AGE and can contribute to the authors' understanding of immune response after natural infection and potentially help identify correlates of protection against severe norovirus disease.

source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Tasso self-collection blood kits have been validated against venous blood-derived serum samples, but not for studies of acute gastroenteritis (AGE). The authors' objectives were to describe the performance of the Tasso+ for self-collection of blood samples among adults and children enrolled in a study of medically attended AGE and to describe specimen processing and antibody testing success. METHODS: The authors used the Tasso+ device for self-collection of blood samples within a prospective cohort study at Kaiser Permanente Northwest. RESULTS: Of a total of 1353 adults and 93 children, 63% of adults and 61% of children returned a blood specimen. Of these, 88% were deemed viable for processing, and 100% of viable specimens were of sufficient volume and quality to be processed and assessed for norovirus antibodies. title: Changing seasonality and trends of other infectious diarrhea and norovirus across the pandemic era in Shenzhen China
abstract: Other infectious diarrhea (OID) is a heterogeneous surveillance syndrome whose temporal patterns may change with transmission, pathogen composition, care seeking and reporting. We analyzed 578,222 OID reports from Shenzhen, China, from 1 January 2013 to 31 July 2025, together with monthly norovirus GI-positive, GII-positive and mixed GI + GII-positive series. Calendar-month distributions differed across pre-COVID-19, during COVID-19 and post-COVID-19 periods for all four series. Autocorrelation-aware breakpoint profiling with adjustment for temperature, relative humidity and wet-day frequency favored February 2020, whereas independent-error profiling favored January 2022. In the primary climate-adjusted ARMA(2,0) model, OID reports fell 48.1% at February 2020, then increased by 2.15% per month. The slope change was 1.13% per month, with a confidence interval spanning zero. A January 2022 sensitivity model estimated a positive post-break trend of 3.28% per month, but its slope change also included zero. A three-segment model found no additional acceleration in January 2022 relative to 2020–2021. Available meteorological covariates did not explain the positive later trend. These findings support changing surveillance dynamics across the COVID-19 era, but not a unique or causal 2022 acceleration.

title_zh: 中国深圳疫情期间其他感染性腹泻和诺如病毒的季节性变化和趋势
source_body_en: Other infectious diarrhea (OID) is a heterogeneous surveillance syndrome whose temporal patterns may change with transmission, pathogen composition, care seeking and reporting. We analyzed 578,222 OID reports from Shenzhen, China, from 1 January 2013 to 31 July 2025, together with monthly norovirus GI-positive, GII-positive and mixed GI + GII-positive series. Calendar-month distributions differed across pre-COVID-19, during COVID-19 and post-COVID-19 periods for all four series. Autocorrelation-aware breakpoint profiling with adjustment for temperature, relative humidity and wet-day frequency favored February 2020, whereas independent-error profiling favored January 2022. In the primary climate-adjusted ARMA(2,0) model, OID reports fell 48.1% at February 2020, then increased by 2.15% per month. The slope change was 1.13% per month, with a confidence interval spanning zero. A January 2022 sensitivity model estimated a positive post-break trend of 3.28% per month, but its slope change also included zero. A three-segment model found no additional acceleration in January 2022 relative to 2020–2021. Available meteorological covariates did not explain the positive later trend. These findings support changing surveillance dynamics across the COVID-19 era, but not a unique or causal 2022 acceleration.

title: Symmetry-breaking antibody binding reveals extensive capsid malleability in pandemic human norovirus
abstract: Virus capsids are metastable assemblies with an exquisite balance between stability and flexibility, obligatory for entry, infectivity, and immune escape. Yet the extent to which human viruses exploit capsid plasticity and how that consequently shapes antigenic landscapes remains poorly understood. Human noroviruses (HuNoVs) are the leading cause of acute viral gastroenteritis worldwide. GII.4 HuNoVs have been evolving epochally, driving most global pandemics, and since 2012, GII.4 Sydney has been the dominant variant. The major capsid protein, VP1, is central to infectivity and immune recognition, and VP1-based virus-like particles (VLPs) are considered promising vaccine candidates. Yet, how the icosahedral HuNoV capsid responds to antibody pressure at the atomic level remains unclear. Here, we present the first atomic structure of GII.4 Sydney capsid determined by cryo-EM, revealing the structural features that likely contribute to its sustained dominance. Using focused refinement, we uncover the remarkable capsid plasticity in response to symmetry-breaking binding of neutralizing and non-neutralizing antibodies. VP1 adopts 11 distinct conformational modalities to accommodate asymmetric antibody binding, and antibody-disrupted VLPs reassemble into smaller particles with five additional VP1 states. This previously unrecognized extent of conformational adaptability provides key insights for designing next-generation VLP- or mRNA-based vaccines targeting HuNoV infections.

abstract_original: Virus capsids are metastable assemblies with an exquisite balance between stability and flexibility, obligatory for entry, infectivity, and immune escape. Yet the extent to which human viruses exploit capsid plasticity and how that consequently shapes antigenic landscapes remains poorly understood. Human noroviruses (HuNoVs) are the leading cause of acute viral gastroenteritis worldwide. GII.4 HuNoVs have been evolving epochally, driving most global pandemics, and since 2012, GII.4 Sydney has been the dominant variant. The major capsid protein, VP1, is central to infectivity and immune recognition, and VP1-based virus-like particles (VLPs) are considered promising vaccine candidates. Yet, how the icosahedral HuNoV capsid responds to antibody pressure at the atomic level remains unclear. Here, we present the first atomic structure of GII.4 Sydney capsid determined by cryo-EM, revealing the structural features that likely contribute to its sustained dominance. title: Clinical complications during hospitalizations of all-cause and norovirus acute gastroenteritis among adults in the United States, 2022–2024
abstract: Abstract Background Although norovirus is the leading cause of acute gastroenteritis (AGE) globally, contemporary data describing the clinical spectrum of hospitalized all-cause and norovirus-associated AGE are limited. We characterized clinical complications during acute hospitalizations among adults with all-cause and norovirus AGE. Methods We conducted a descriptive study using Optum’s de-identified Clinformatics ® Data Mart (Optum® CDM) administrative claims database. Adults aged ≥ 18 years with hospitalized all-cause AGE or norovirus-specified episodes between July 2022 and June 2024 were identified using ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes. Clinical complications during acute hospitalizations occurring within 3 days of the index episode were evaluated by age group (18–59 and ≥ 60 years) and presence of underlying medical conditions. Baseline frailty among adults aged ≥ 60 years was assessed using a validated claims-based frailty index. Results The study included 192,430 hospitalized all-cause AGE episodes and 2,589 hospitalized norovirus-coded episodes. Patients were predominantly older adults (median age, 74 years) with multiple underlying medical conditions. Metabolic disturbances, acute kidney injury, dehydration, and sepsis were the most common complications among patients with all-cause AGE (57.2%, 38.3%, 29.2%, and 26.5%, respectively) or norovirus-coded episodes (62.0%, 42.6%, 41.9%, and 28.1%, respectively). High frequencies of complications were also observed among younger adults with norovirus hospitalizations. Among adults aged ≥ 60 years, baseline frailty was substantially higher among patients with underlying medical conditions than among those without. Conclusions Hospitalized adults with all-cause and norovirus-coded AGE commonly experienced renal, metabolic, and systemic complications. Older adults demonstrated substantial baseline frailty, while severe complications also occurred among younger adults hospitalized with norovirus illness. These findings improve the clinical characterization of severe AGE, specifically norovirus, and identify populations at greatest risk for adverse outcomes.

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,患有全因和 诺如病毒 编码 AGE 的住院成人通常会出现肾脏、代谢和全身并发症。这些发现改善了严重 AGE(特别是 诺如病毒)的临床特征,并确定了不良结果风险最大的人群。

analysis_zh.main_results: 该研究包括 192,430 例住院的全因 AGE 发作和 2,589 例住院的 诺如病毒 编码发作。代谢紊乱、急性肾损伤、脱水和脓毒症是全因 AGE(分别为 57.2%、38.3%、29.2% 和 26.5%)或 诺如病毒 编码发作(分别为 62.0%、42.6%、41.9% 和 28.1%)患者中最常见的并发症。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,患有全因和 诺如病毒 编码 AGE 的住院成人通常会出现肾脏、代谢和全身并发症。这些发现改善了严重 AGE(特别是 诺如病毒)的临床特征,并确定了不良结果风险最大的人群。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为有针对性的 监测 和严重 AGE 的风险评估提供信息,特别是在 诺如病毒 感染的成年人中,并强调需要改进高危人群的临床管理和预防策略。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其依赖行政索赔数据而受到限制,这可能会引入偏差并缺乏详细的临床信息。证据是中等的,因为它提供了对并发症的描述性见解,但没有建立因果关系。

title: The third study of infectious intestinal disease in the community: microbiological methods
abstract: Infectious intestinal disease (IID) is a significant public health concern, with an estimated 17 million cases occurring annually in the UK. The third study of IID in the community (IID3 study) will provide updated estimates of the incidence and aetiology of IID in the UK. This protocol describes the laboratory methods employed by the IID3 study in primary diagnostic and reference laboratories. Stool specimens were obtained from subjects in the UK with symptoms of IID who were prospectively enrolled through primary care in two cohorts from May 2023 to September 2025. Specimens were tested for 21 pathogens using PCR-based methods in two separate workflows at Liverpool Clinical Laboratories. The first workflow comprised EntericBio DX, Viral Panel 3 and Clostridium difficile assays (Serosep, Crawley, UK); and the second a panel of assays for detection of Clostridium perfringens (cpa), Aeromonas spp ., Cyclospora cayetanensis and diarrhoeagenic Escherichia coli based on 3base ® Technology [Genetic Signatures (GS), Newtown, Australia]. Specimens that tested positive for Salmonella spp ., Campylobacter spp ., Yersinia spp ., Vibrio spp ., Shigella spp. and diarrhoeagenic E. coli were referred together with the corresponding bacterial isolate to the Gastrointestinal Bacteria Reference Unit, UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) for whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing. Samples that tested positive for Cryptosporidium spp., Giardia duodenalis and Cyclospora cayetanensis were referred for genotyping to the national Cryptosporidium Reference Unit, Public Health Wales. Norovirus-positive faecal specimens were referred for Sanger sequencing-based genotyping to the Enteric Virus Unit, UKHSA. These methods encompassing modern diagnostic and reference microbiology represent a comprehensive approach to the detection and characterization of pathogens causing IID in the UK population and serve as a reference for future studies.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究将从英国患有 IID 症状的受试者中获取粪便标本,这些受试者在 2023 年 5 月至 2025 年 9 月期间通过初级保健前瞻性地入组了两个 队列研究。
elements_zh.methods: 利物浦临床实验室使用基于 PCR 的方法在两个独立的工作流程中对样本进行了 21 种病原体检测。第一个工作流程包括 EntericBio DX、Viral Panel 3 和艰难梭菌检测(Serosep,Crawley,英国);第二个是基于 3base ® 技术 [Genetic Signatures (GS),Newtown,澳大利亚] 检测产气荚膜梭菌 (cpa)、气单胞菌、卡耶坦环孢子菌和致泻大肠杆菌的一组检测。
elements_zh.main_results: 这些方法涵盖现代诊断和参考微生物学,代表了在英国人群中检测和表征引起 IID 的病原体的综合方法,并可作为未来研究的参考。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究将提供英国 发病率 和 IID 病因学的最新估计,为病原体的检测和表征提供全面的方法。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果将告知 IID 的 监测、诊断 和 治疗,为英国的公共卫生工作做出贡献。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到初级保健前瞻性受试者招募的限制,这可能无法代表整个英国人口。证据强度中等。

title: HIRSCHSPRUNG DISEASE: WHEN BOWEL DYSFUNCTION TAKES A SYSTEMIC TURN - A CASE REPORT
abstract: Background: Hirschsprung disease (HD) is a rare congenital disorder of the enteric nervous system, caused by impaired neural crest cell migration during intestinal development. This leads to aganglionosis of the distal bowel, most frequently affecting the rectosigmoid colon. Its most feared complication is the Hirschsprung-associated Enterocolitis (HAEC), the leading cause of mortality and morbidity. Case presentation: A 4-year-old boy, with a history of HD treated two years prior with a Swenson pull-through procedure, presented to the paediatric emergency department with a one-day history of abdominal pain, fetid diarrhoea, and vomiting. No other symptoms were recorded. Physical examination revealed no abnormalities. Oral antiemetics and hydration were administered. During hospitalization, he remained lethargic with progressive abdominal distension, for which intravenous fluids were initiated for maintenance and replacement of ongoing losses. Initial laboratory tests and blood cultures were unremarkable. Gastrointestinal molecular panel was positive for norovirus, with a negative stool culture. Abdominal radiography showed marked dilatation of bowel loops and faecal loading (Figure 1). Within six hours, he deteriorated rapidly with the onset of fever, tachycardia, signs of poor peripheral perfusion, and hypotension. Laboratory reassessment showed severe metabolic acidosis (pH and HCO3 below the measurable range), hyperlactatemia (9.8 mmol/L), acute kidney injury (creatinine 0.9 mg/dL; 2.25-fold increase from baseline), and elevated inflammatory markers (C-reactive protein 27.7 mg/dL and procalcitonin >100 ng/mL), findings consistent with severe HAEC presenting with mixed hypovolemic/septic shock. Resuscitation required a total of 60 mL/kg of crystalloid boluses, and ceftriaxone and metronidazole were started. Gastrointestinal decompression was performed via nasogastric tube placement, with drainage of faecal material, and rectal enema, with explosive discharge of stools. He was transferred to the paediatric intensive care unit. Further stabilization required three additional crystalloid boluses and aggressive fluid therapy (up to 3500 mL/m2/day), supplemented with calcium and potassium, without the need for vasoactive support. Antibiotics were adjusted to cefotaxime, metronidazole, and gentamicin. Serial rectal irrigations were performed, with abundant faecal output. Gastric residual progressively decreased, alongside marked improvement in abdominal distension. The patient was discharged after 12 days, clinically and analytically stable, with normalization of renal function. Discussion: HAEC is a complication which may happen both before and after surgery, in 20-40% of HD patients. A high index of clinical suspicion is required for timely diagnosis and management. During the initial stages, clinical presentation is non-specific and can mimic acute gastroenteritis. However, patients may rapidly progress to mixed hypovolemic/distributive (septic) shock. Management relies on aggressive fluid therapy for haemodynamic stabilization and gastrointestinal source control. Broad-spectrum antibiotics are mandatory for seven to ten days, with coverage of anaerobes and enteric gram-negative organisms. Gastrointestinal decompression is crucial, with nasogastric tube placement, serial rectal irrigations, and bowel rest. If medical management is not sufficient, or in case of bowel perforation, peritonitis or pneumatosis, surgery might be needed. In this case, HAEC (Pastor/Delphi HAEC score of 11) occurred two years after surgery, likely triggered by norovirus infection.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 先天性巨结肠症(HD)是一种罕见的肠神经系统先天性疾病,由肠道发育过程中神经嵴细胞迁移受损引起。这会导致远端肠神经节缺失,最常影响直肠乙状结肠。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是 病例报告 的研究,描述了一名有 HD 病史的 4 岁男孩,两年前接受了 Swenson 拔出手术治疗。他因一天腹痛、恶臭腹泻和呕吐病史到儿科急诊科就诊。没有记录到其他症状。
elements_zh.methods: 给予口服止吐药和水化。在住院期间,他仍然昏昏欲睡,并伴有进行性腹胀,为此开始静脉输液以维持和补充持续的损失。最初的实验室测试和血培养没有异常。胃肠道分子检测 诺如病毒 呈阳性,粪便培养呈阴性。通过放置鼻胃管进行胃肠减压,引流粪便物质,并进行直肠灌肠,将粪便爆炸性排出。
elements_zh.main_results: 腹部X光检查显示肠袢明显扩张和粪便负荷。实验室重新评估显示严重代谢性酸中毒(pH 和 HCO3 低于可测量范围)、高乳酸血症(9.8 mmol/L)、急性肾损伤(肌酐 0.9 mg/dL;较基线增加 2.25 倍)和炎症标志物升高(C 反应蛋白 27.7 mg/dL 和降钙素原 >100 ng/mL),这些结果与表现为混合性严重 HAEC 一致。低血容量/感染性休克。胃残留逐渐减少,腹胀明显改善。12 天后,患者出院,临床和分析结果稳定,肾功能正常。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: HAEC 是一种并发症,20-40% 的 HD 患者在手术前后都可能发生。在初始阶段,临床表现是非特异性的,可以模仿 急性胃肠炎。然而,患者可能会迅速进展为混合性低血容量/分布性(脓毒性)休克。治疗依靠积极的液体治疗来稳定血流动力学和控制胃肠源头。广谱抗生素必须使用七到十天,覆盖厌氧菌和肠道革兰氏阴性菌。胃肠减压至关重要,包括放置鼻胃管、连续直肠冲洗和肠道休息。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 及时的 诊断 和管理需要高度的临床怀疑。研究结果强调了认识到 HAEC 作为 HD 患者潜在并发症的重要性,即使在手术干预后也是如此,并强调需要采取迅速和积极的 治疗 策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据并未报告局限性。该证据基于单个 病例报告,其通用性有限。然而,研究结果与 HAEC 和 诺如病毒 感染的已知临床表现一致,支持适度的置信度评估。

title_zh: 先天性巨结肠症:当肠功能障碍发生系统性转变时 - 病例报告
source_body_en: Background: Hirschsprung disease (HD) is a rare congenital disorder of the enteric nervous system, caused by impaired neural crest cell migration during intestinal development. This leads to aganglionosis of the distal bowel, most frequently affecting the rectosigmoid colon. Its most feared complication is the Hirschsprung-associated Enterocolitis (HAEC), the leading cause of mortality and morbidity. Case presentation: A 4-year-old boy, with a history of HD treated two years prior with a Swenson pull-through procedure, presented to the paediatric emergency department with a one-day history of abdominal pain, fetid diarrhoea, and vomiting. No other symptoms were recorded. Physical examination revealed no abnormalities. Oral antiemetics and hydration were administered. During hospitalization, he remained lethargic with progressive abdominal distension, for which intravenous fluids were initiated for maintenance and replacement of ongoing losses. Initial laboratory tests and blood cultures were unremarkable. Gastrointestinal molecular panel was positive for norovirus, with a negative stool culture. Abdominal radiography showed marked dilatation of bowel loops and faecal loading (Figure 1). Within six hours, he deteriorated rapidly with the onset of fever, tachycardia, signs of poor peripheral perfusion, and hypotension. Laboratory reassessment showed severe metabolic acidosis (pH and HCO3 below the measurable range), hyperlactatemia (9.8 mmol/L), acute kidney injury (creatinine 0.9 mg/dL; 2.25-fold increase from baseline), and elevated inflammatory markers (C-reactive protein 27.7 mg/dL and procalcitonin >100 ng/mL), findings consistent with severe HAEC presenting with mixed hypovolemic/septic shock. Resuscitation required a total of 60 mL/kg of crystalloid boluses, and ceftriaxone and metronidazole were started. Gastrointestinal decompression was performed via nasogastric tube placement, with drainage of faecal material, and rectal enema, with explosive discharge of stools. He was transferred to the paediatric intensive care unit. Further stabilization required three additional crystalloid boluses and aggressive fluid therapy (up to 3500 mL/m2/day), supplemented with calcium and potassium, without the need for vasoactive support. Antibiotics were adjusted to cefotaxime, metronidazole, and gentamicin. Serial rectal irrigations were performed, with abundant faecal output. Gastric residual progressively decreased, alongside marked improvement in abdominal distension. The patient was discharged after 12 days, clinically and analytically stable, with normalization of renal function. Discussion: HAEC is a complication which may happen both before and after surgery, in 20-40% of HD patients. A high index of clinical suspicion is required for timely diagnosis and management. During the initial stages, clinical presentation is non-specific and can mimic acute gastroenteritis. However, patients may rapidly progress to mixed hypovolemic/distributive (septic) shock. Management relies on aggressive fluid therapy for haemodynamic stabilization and gastrointestinal source control. Broad-spectrum antibiotics are mandatory for seven to ten days, with coverage of anaerobes and enteric gram-negative organisms. Gastrointestinal decompression is crucial, with nasogastric tube placement, serial rectal irrigations, and bowel rest. If medical management is not sufficient, or in case of bowel perforation, peritonitis or pneumatosis, surgery might be needed. In this case, HAEC (Pastor/Delphi HAEC score of 11) occurred two years after surgery, likely triggered by norovirus infection.
abstract_zh: 背景:先天性巨结肠症(HD)是一种罕见的肠神经系统先天性疾病,由肠道发育过程中神经嵴细胞迁移受损引起。这会导致远端肠神经节缺失,最常影响直肠乙状结肠。其最可怕的并发症是先天性巨结肠相关小肠结肠炎 (HAEC),它是 死亡率 和发病率的主要原因。病例介绍:一名 4 岁男孩,有 HD 病史,两年前接受过 Swenson 拉通手术治疗,因一天腹痛、恶臭腹泻和呕吐而被送往儿科急诊科。没有记录到其他症状。体检未发现异常。给予口服止吐药和水化。在住院期间,他仍然昏昏欲睡,并伴有进行性腹胀,为此开始静脉输液以维持和补充持续的损失。最初的实验室测试和血培养没有异常。胃肠道分子检测 诺如病毒 呈阳性,粪便培养呈阴性。腹部X光检查显示肠袢和粪便明显扩张(图1)。六个小时内,他的病情迅速恶化,出现发烧、心动过速、外周灌注不良的症状和低血压。实验室重新评估显示严重代谢性酸中毒(pH 和 HCO3 低于可测量范围)、高乳酸血症(9.8 mmol/L)、急性肾损伤(肌酐 0.9 mg/dL;较基线增加 2.25 倍)和炎症标志物升高(C 反应蛋白 27.7 mg/dL 和降钙素原 >100 ng/mL),这些结果与表现为混合性严重 HAEC 一致。低血容量/感染性休克。复苏需要总共 60 mL/kg 的晶体推注,并开始使用头孢曲松和甲硝唑。通过放置鼻胃管进行胃肠减压,引流粪便物质,并进行直肠灌肠,将粪便爆炸性排出。他被转移到儿科重症监护室。进一步稳定需要额外的三次晶体推注和积极的液体治疗(高达 3500 mL/m2/天),并补充钙和钾,而不需要血管活性支持。抗生素调整为头孢噻肟、甲硝唑、庆大霉素。进行了连续直肠冲洗,排出了大量粪便。胃残留逐渐减少,腹胀明显改善。12 天后,患者出院,临床和分析结果稳定,肾功能正常。讨论:HAEC 是一种并发症,20-40% 的 HD 患者在手术前后都可能发生。及时的 诊断 和管理需要高度的临床怀疑。在初始阶段,临床表现是非特异性的,可以模仿 急性胃肠炎。然而,患者可能会迅速进展为混合性低血容量/分布性(脓毒性)休克。治疗依靠积极的液体治疗来稳定血流动力学和控制胃肠源头。广谱抗生素必须使用七到十天,覆盖厌氧菌和肠道革兰氏阴性菌。胃肠减压至关重要,包括放置鼻胃管、连续直肠冲洗和肠道休息。如果医疗管理不充分,或者出现肠穿孔、腹膜炎或积气,则可能需要手术。在本例中,HAEC(Pastor/Delphi HAEC 评分为 11)发生在手术两年后,可能是由 诺如病毒 感染引发的。

title: Eculizumab Therapy in Suspected Late-Onset Atypical Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome in an Adult Kidney Transplant Recipient: A Case Report
abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: Atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (aHUS) is a rare, life-threatening, complement-mediated thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA) that may occur de novo after kidney transplantation. Because its manifestations overlap with more common causes of allograft dysfunction, including rejection, calcineurin inhibitor toxicity, and infection, diagnosis can be challenging. The disease may progress rapidly, making early clinical suspicion and timely etiologic evaluation essential. Case Presentation: We report a 52-year-old man who developed abrupt, severe graft dysfunction approximately 10 years after ABO-incompatible living-donor kidney transplantation. His serum creatinine had remained approximately 2.0 mg/dL after treatment for suspected chronic active antibody-mediated rejection but increased to 6.57 mg/dL at outpatient follow-up and to 8.47 mg/dL on admission after a recent norovirus infection. Initial evaluation considered common post-transplant causes of graft dysfunction, including rejection, calcineurin inhibitor toxicity, and infection-related injury. However, as renal dysfunction progressed and concurrent anemia and thrombocytopenia became evident, TMA was suspected, and a targeted workup was undertaken. Elevated lactate dehydrogenase, decreased haptoglobin, fragmented red blood cells, and allograft biopsy findings supported TMA. No HLA class I or II antibodies were detected, C4d staining was negative, ADAMTS13 activity was preserved, and testing for Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli was negative. Genetic testing identified a heterozygous CFH variant (c.3329G>C, p.Gly1110Ala), classified as a variant of uncertain significance. Based on the clinical, hematologic, and histopathologic findings, suspected aHUS was considered the most likely diagnosis. However, ABMR-associated TMA could not be completely excluded. Plasma exchange was complicated by anaphylaxis, and eculizumab was initiated. Hematologic abnormalities subsequently resolved, although renal function did not recover and the patient remained dialysis-dependent. Conclusions: This case highlights the importance of considering TMA when graft dysfunction progresses rapidly or remains unexplained, even many years after kidney transplantation. Early recognition of microangiopathic features and prompt evaluation for the underlying etiology are particularly important when complement-mediated aHUS is suspected, because established acute-on-chronic allograft injury may limit renal recovery despite hematologic response to C5 inhibition.

title_zh: 依库丽单抗治疗成年肾移植受者疑似晚发型非典型溶血性尿毒症综合征:病例报告
source_body_en: Background and Clinical Significance: Atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (aHUS) is a rare, life-threatening, complement-mediated thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA) that may occur de novo after kidney transplantation. Because its manifestations overlap with more common causes of allograft dysfunction, including rejection, calcineurin inhibitor toxicity, and infection, diagnosis can be challenging. The disease may progress rapidly, making early clinical suspicion and timely etiologic evaluation essential. Case Presentation: We report a 52-year-old man who developed abrupt, severe graft dysfunction approximately 10 years after ABO-incompatible living-donor kidney transplantation. His serum creatinine had remained approximately 2.0 mg/dL after treatment for suspected chronic active antibody-mediated rejection but increased to 6.57 mg/dL at outpatient follow-up and to 8.47 mg/dL on admission after a recent norovirus infection. Initial evaluation considered common post-transplant causes of graft dysfunction, including rejection, calcineurin inhibitor toxicity, and infection-related injury. However, as renal dysfunction progressed and concurrent anemia and thrombocytopenia became evident, TMA was suspected, and a targeted workup was undertaken. Elevated lactate dehydrogenase, decreased haptoglobin, fragmented red blood cells, and allograft biopsy findings supported TMA. No HLA class I or II antibodies were detected, C4d staining was negative, ADAMTS13 activity was preserved, and testing for Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli was negative. Genetic testing identified a heterozygous CFH variant (c.3329G>C, p.Gly1110Ala), classified as a variant of uncertain significance. Based on the clinical, hematologic, and histopathologic findings, suspected aHUS was considered the most likely diagnosis. However, ABMR-associated TMA could not be completely excluded. Plasma exchange was complicated by anaphylaxis, and eculizumab was initiated. Hematologic abnormalities subsequently resolved, although renal function did not recover and the patient remained dialysis-dependent. Conclusions: This case highlights the importance of considering TMA when graft dysfunction progresses rapidly or remains unexplained, even many years after kidney transplantation. Early recognition of microangiopathic features and prompt evaluation for the underlying etiology are particularly important when complement-mediated aHUS is suspected, because established acute-on-chronic allograft injury may limit renal recovery despite hematologic response to C5 inhibition.
abstract_zh: 背景和临床意义:非典型溶血性尿毒症综合征(aHUS)是一种罕见的、危及生命的、补体介导的血栓性微血管病(TMA),可能在肾移植后重新发生。由于其表现与同种异体移植功能障碍的更常见原因重叠,包括排斥、钙调神经磷酸酶抑制剂毒性和感染,诊断 可能具有挑战性。该疾病可能进展迅速,因此早期临床怀疑和及时的病因学评估至关重要。病例介绍:我们报告一名 52 岁男性,在 ABO 血型不合的活体供体肾移植后约 10 年后突然出现严重的移植物功能障碍。由于疑似慢性活动性抗体介导的排斥反应,在 治疗 治疗后,他的血清肌酐仍保持在约 2.0 mg/dL,但在门诊随访时增加至 6.57 mg/dL,在最近的 诺如病毒 感染后入院时增加至 8.47 mg/dL。初步评估考虑了移植物功能障碍的常见移植后原因,包括排斥、钙调神经磷酸酶抑制剂毒性和感染相关损伤。然而,随着肾功能障碍的进展以及并发贫血和血小板减少症变得明显,怀疑是TMA,并进行了有针对性的检查。乳酸脱氢酶升高、触珠蛋白降低、红细胞碎片和同种异体移植物活检结果支持 TMA。未检测到 HLA I 类或 II 类抗体,C4d 染色呈阴性,ADAMTS13 活性得以保留,产志贺毒素大肠杆菌检测呈阴性。基因检测发现了杂合 CFH 变异(c.3329G>C,p.Gly1110Ala),被归类为意义不确定的变异。根据临床、血液学和组织病理学结果,怀疑 aHUS 被认为是最有可能的 诊断。然而,不能完全排除 ABMR 相关的 TMA。过敏反应使血浆置换变得复杂,因此开始使用依库丽单抗。尽管肾功能没有恢复并且患者仍然依赖透析,但血液学异常随后得到解决。结论:该病例凸显了当移植物功能障碍迅速进展或仍无法解释时(甚至在肾移植后多年)考虑 TMA 的重要性。当怀疑补体介导的 aHUS 时,早期识别微血管病变特征并及时评估潜在病因尤其重要,因为尽管对 C5 抑制有血液学反应,但已确定的慢性同种异体移植物急性损伤可能会限制肾脏恢复。

full_text: Described as the “Ferrari of the virus world” for the way it races from person to person, norovirus is once again on the move as we head into winter. Reports from the UK Health Security Agency have highlighted that cases of norovirus – commonly known as the “winter vomiting bug” – have increased by more than 35% in England over the past two weeks, compared with the previous fortnight. While that sounds alarming, this is still within expected levels for the season. Overall case numbers are about 5% above what’s typical for this time of year. Cases have fallen in Scotland, but Wales has seen a rise. Norovirus symptoms include sudden-onset nausea, diarrhoea and vomiting, sometimes accompanied by fever, stomach pain, body aches and headaches. Most healthy adults recover within one to three days. However, those with weakened immune systems, older adults and young children face a higher risk of severe symptoms. When this happens, people can be ill for much longer and may need hospital treatment if they become dehydrated. Norovirus is highly contagious, with some studies suggesting that as few as ten virus particles can cause an infection. It spreads from person to person when tiny amounts of virus from infected faeces or vomit get on to food, hands or surfaces and are then transferred to the mouth. Close contact between people can also spread the virus. This may help explain why cases peak in winter, when people spend more time together indoors. However, you can catch it at any time of the year. The virus is also particularly resilient; it can survive on hard kitchen surfaces such as stainless steel and ceramic for up to two weeks, and it takes temperatures of around 60°C to kill it. There are no approved vaccines or specific treatments for norovirus. It evolves quickly to escape our immune systems, and has proved notoriously difficult to grow in the lab, which has hampered research efforts. That said, recent breakthroughs in growing norovirus using lab-grown human gut cells may make it easier to develop treatments in future. How to protect yourself and your household While alcohol-based hand sanitisers can be effective against other viruses, such as the ones that cause COVID and flu, they don’t work well against norovirus. Instead, the best way to protect yourself is by washing your hands often with soap and hot water, ideally for 15 seconds or more. This is particularly important before or after preparing food, and after going to the toilet. Norovirus is also frequently spread through contaminated food. Fresh produce such as fruit and vegetables may pick up the virus during harvesting, packaging or handling, so wash these thoroughly before use. Shellfish such as oysters can also be contaminated with concentrated norovirus from the water they live in, so ensure these are thoroughly cooked, rather than steamed or eaten raw. If someone in your household has norovirus, cleaning surfaces regularly with bleach-based products can help prevent the virus from spreading. Using a dummy called Vomiting Larry, researchers found that norovirus-containing droplets can spread around ten feet (three metres) when someone vomits. So, it’s important to immediately clean areas that have been contaminated by vomit or faeces. Frequent cleaning of heavily used surfaces such as door handles, light switches, taps, toilet seats and flush handles, ideally while wearing disposable gloves, can help reduce the chances of the virus spreading. Washing soiled clothes or bedding separately from other laundry, at a temperature of 60°C or above at the longest cycle time possible, can also help kill the virus on soft surfaces. If you are unlucky enough to get norovirus yourself, the only solution is to allow the virus to run its short, but deeply unpleasant, course. Replacing lost fluids is essential, so drink plenty of water, tea or electrolyte drinks, or use oral rehydration sachets. If you feel able to eat, stick to plain foods that are easy to digest, such as toast, rice, pasta or soup, and avoid fatty or salty foods that may make your symptoms worse. As norovirus is highly contagious, ensure that you stay at home and rest as much as possible. Keep your distance from other people in your household where you can, and avoid preparing food for others while you’re unwell and for at least 48 hours after symptoms stop. full_text_sections.full_text: Described as the “Ferrari of the virus world” for the way it races from person to person, norovirus is once again on the move as we head into winter. Reports from the UK Health Security Agency have highlighted that cases of norovirus – commonly known as the “winter vomiting bug” – have increased by more than 35% in England over the past two weeks, compared with the previous fortnight. While that sounds alarming, this is still within expected levels for the season. Overall case numbers are about 5% above what’s typical for this time of year. Cases have fallen in Scotland, but Wales has seen a rise. Norovirus symptoms include sudden-onset nausea, diarrhoea and vomiting, sometimes accompanied by fever, stomach pain, body aches and headaches. Most healthy adults recover within one to three days. However, those with weakened immune systems, older adults and young children face a higher risk of severe symptoms. When this happens, people can be ill for much longer and may need hospital treatment if they become dehydrated. Norovirus is highly contagious, with some studies suggesting that as few as ten virus particles can cause an infection. It spreads from person to person when tiny amounts of virus from infected faeces or vomit get on to food, hands or surfaces and are then transferred to the mouth. Close contact between people can also spread the virus. This may help explain why cases peak in winter, when people spend more time together indoors. However, you can catch it at any time of the year. The virus is also particularly resilient; it can survive on hard kitchen surfaces such as stainless steel and ceramic for up to two weeks, and it takes temperatures of around 60°C to kill it. There are no approved vaccines or specific treatments for norovirus. It evolves quickly to escape our immune systems, and has proved notoriously difficult to grow in the lab, which has hampered research efforts. That said, recent breakthroughs in growing norovirus using lab-grown human gut cells may make it easier to develop treatments in future. How to protect yourself and your household While alcohol-based hand sanitisers can be effective against other viruses, such as the ones that cause COVID and flu, they don’t work well against norovirus. Instead, the best way to protect yourself is by washing your hands often with soap and hot water, ideally for 15 seconds or more. This is particularly important before or after preparing food, and after going to the toilet. Norovirus is also frequently spread through contaminated food. Fresh produce such as fruit and vegetables may pick up the virus during harvesting, packaging or handling, so wash these thoroughly before use. Shellfish such as oysters can also be contaminated with concentrated norovirus from the water they live in, so ensure these are thoroughly cooked, rather than steamed or eaten raw. If someone in your household has norovirus, cleaning surfaces regularly with bleach-based products can help prevent the virus from spreading. Using a dummy called Vomiting Larry, researchers found that norovirus-containing droplets can spread around ten feet (three metres) when someone vomits. So, it’s important to immediately clean areas that have been contaminated by vomit or faeces. Frequent cleaning of heavily used surfaces such as door handles, light switches, taps, toilet seats and flush handles, ideally while wearing disposable gloves, can help reduce the chances of the virus spreading. Washing soiled clothes or bedding separately from other laundry, at a temperature of 60°C or above at the longest cycle time possible, can also help kill the virus on soft surfaces. If you are unlucky enough to get norovirus yourself, the only solution is to allow the virus to run its short, but deeply unpleasant, course. Replacing lost fluids is essential, so drink plenty of water, tea or electrolyte drinks, or use oral rehydration sachets. If you feel able to eat, stick to plain foods that are easy to digest, such as toast, rice, pasta or soup, and avoid fatty or salty foods that may make your symptoms worse. As norovirus is highly contagious, ensure that you stay at home and rest as much as possible. Keep your distance from other people in your household where you can, and avoid preparing food for others while you’re unwell and for at least 48 hours after symptoms stop. Even after full recovery, infectious virus can still be shed in poo for up to two weeks, so continuing to frequently clean bathroom areas can help prevent further transmission. With cases rising as winter sets in, the Ferrari of viruses may be doing the rounds for a while yet. A few simple habits could save you, and others, a very unpleasant few days.

title_original: Norovirus is spreading – how to recognise the symptoms and what to do

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the spread of norovirus and its associated symptoms, highlighting the need for awareness and understanding of its seasonal patterns and public health impact. The background emphasized the virus's rapid transmission and its designation as the "Ferrari of the virus world.".
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed reported cases of norovirus in England, Scotland, and Wales over the past two weeks, comparing them to typical seasonal levels. It noted that case numbers in England have increased by more than 35% compared to the previous fortnight, while Scotland has seen a decline and Wales an increase.
analysis.methods: The study relied on data from the UK Health Security Agency, tracking reported cases of norovirus across different regions. It also discussed the virus's transmission mechanisms, including its ability to spread through contaminated surfaces and close contact, and its resilience to heat.
analysis.main_results: Reports from the UK Health Security Agency indicate that norovirus cases in England have increased by more than 35% over the past two weeks, with overall case numbers about 5% above typical seasonal levels. Cases have fallen in Scotland but risen in Wales.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the rise in cases as consistent with seasonal expectations, suggesting that the increase in England may be due to factors like increased indoor contact during winter. They noted that the virus's resilience and rapid evolution pose challenges for research and control efforts.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform public health strategies for norovirus surveillance and prevention, particularly in settings where close contact is common. They also highlight the need for continued research into developing treatments and vaccines due to the virus's rapid evolution and lab-growth difficulties.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on reported case data, which may not capture all instances of norovirus infection. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on observational data rather than controlled experiments.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the recent spread of norovirus in England, Scotland, and Wales, noting a 35% increase in cases over the past two weeks compared to the previous fortnight. While overall case numbers are slightly above seasonal norms, Scotland has seen a decline, and Wales an increase. The paper highlights norovirus's rapid transmission, symptoms, and the challenges in developing treatments due to its quick evolution and difficulty in lab cultivation. It also discusses the virus's resilience to heat and its spread through contaminated surfaces and close contact. The findings suggest that the rise in cases may be linked to increased indoor interactions during winter, but the evidence is moderate due to reliance on observational data. The study underscores the importance of continued surveillance and research into norovirus, given its public health impact and the lack of approved vaccines or treatments.

Arts + Culture Economy Education Environment + Energy Ethics + Religion Health Politics + Society Science + Tech World Podcasts Local Prostock-studio/Shutterstock.com Norovirus is spreading – how to recognise the symptoms and what to do Published: November 24, 2026 6:37am EST Described as the “Ferrari of the virus world” for the way it races from person to person, norovirus is once again on the move as we head into winter. Reports from the UK Health Security Agency have highlighted that cases of norovirus – commonly known as the “winter vomiting bug” – have increased by more than 35% in England over the past two weeks, compared with the previous fortnight. While that sounds alarming, this is still within expected levels for the season. Overall case numbers are about 5% above what’s typical for this time of year. Cases have fallen in Scotland, but Wales has seen a rise. Norovirus symptoms include sudden-onset nausea, diarrhoea and vomiting, sometimes accompanied by fever, stomach pain, body aches and headaches. Most healthy adults recover within one to three days. However, those with weakened immune systems, older adults and young children face a higher risk of severe symptoms. When this happens, people can be ill for much longer and may need hospital treatment if they become dehydrated. Norovirus is highly contagious, with some studies suggesting that as few as ten virus particles can cause an infection. It spreads from person to person when tiny amounts of virus from infected faeces or vomit get on to food, hands or surfaces and are then transferred to the mouth. Close contact between people can also spread the virus. This may help explain why cases peak in winter, when people spend more time together indoors. However, you can catch it at any time of the year. The virus is also particularly resilient; it can survive on hard kitchen surfaces such as stainless steel and ceramic for up to two weeks, and it takes temperatures of around 60°C to kill it. There are no approved vaccines or specific treatments for norovirus. It evolves quickly to escape our immune systems, and has proved notoriously difficult to grow in the lab, which has hampered research efforts. That said, recent breakthroughs in growing norovirus using lab-grown human gut cells may make it easier to develop treatments in future. How to protect yourself and your household While alcohol-based hand sanitisers can be effective against other viruses, such as the ones that cause COVID and flu, they don’t work well against norovirus. Instead, the best way to protect yourself is by washing your hands often with soap and hot water, ideally for 15 seconds or more. This is particularly important before or after preparing food, and after going to the toilet. Norovirus is also frequently spread through contaminated food. Fresh produce such as fruit and vegetables may pick up the virus during harvesting, packaging or handling, so wash these thoroughly before use. Shellfish such as oysters can also be contaminated with concentrated norovirus from the water they live in, so ensure these are thoroughly cooked, rather than steamed or eaten raw. If someone in your household has norovirus, cleaning surfaces regularly with bleach-based products can help prevent the virus from spreading. Using a dummy called Vomiting Larry, researchers found that norovirus-containing droplets can spread around ten feet (three metres) when someone vomits. So, it’s important to immediately clean areas that have been contaminated by vomit or faeces. Vomiting Larry in action. Frequent cleaning of heavily used surfaces such as door handles, light switches, taps, toilet seats and flush handles, ideally while wearing disposable gloves, can help reduce the chances of the virus spreading. Washing soiled clothes or bedding separately from other laundry, at a temperature of 60°C or above at the longest cycle time possible, can also help kill the virus on soft surfaces. If you are unlucky enough to get norovirus yourself, the only solution is to allow the virus to run its short, but deeply unpleasant, course. Replacing lost fluids is essential, so drink plenty of water, tea or electrolyte drinks, or use oral rehydration sachets. If you feel able to eat, stick to plain foods that are easy to digest, such as toast, rice, pasta or soup, and avoid fatty or salty foods that may make your symptoms worse. As norovirus is highly contagious, ensure that you stay at home and rest as much as possible. Keep your distance from other people in your household where you can, and avoid preparing food for others while you’re unwell and for at least 48 hours after symptoms stop. Even after full recovery, infectious virus can still be shed in poo for up to two weeks, so continuing to frequently clean bathroom areas can help prevent further transmission. With cases rising as winter sets in, the Ferrari of viruses may be doing the rounds for a while yet. A few simple habits could save you, and others, a very unpleasant few days.
